This report is the first step in the process to prioritize the city's 2024-2035 major capital projects.
As previously reported, the first step is to establish guiding principles that will help administration determine what projects to include in a prioritization process and how to prioritize them.
The report outlined six proposed guiding principles to utilize in the next steps of the process.
The first three guiding principles are taken directly from the strategic plan.
Projects that make a significant impact on any of the three strategic pillars,
specifically projects that advanced city council priorities, deliver excellence and course services and operational priorities,
and drive corporate transformational change will be given a higher waiting than those that do not.
Projects that maximize other sources of funding will also be weighted higher than those that don't.
Leveraging the city's available funding to capture private or other levels of government funding will be a key to ensure we maximize the impact of this investment.
The last two priorities relate to limiting the process to civic projects as well as to major projects.
An arbitrary threshold of 2 million has been identified for the purpose of this process to ensure that the prioritized list focuses on those major projects.
Other opportunities such as operating budget existing reserves and RCE all provide opportunities for smaller value projects to be addressed.

If approved, the administration will take these guiding principles back to begin compilation of expected major project pressures from 2024 to 2035 and bring back a suggested priority list of projects to build into future budgets.
Following confirmation of the prioritized list of funding plan and funding options will also be presented to committee.
